readout_other: multi-unit activity and local field potentials (32-channel silicon probe); sharp-wave ripples
direction_notes: Hippocampal firing rate increased during 52 mW/cm2 CW tFUS (modestly at 13 mW/cm2); the increase was larger with low baseline delta and high theta/gamma power and frequent sharp-wave ripples. Olfactory-bulb stimulation and air-gap control produced no significant change.

timing.protocol_description: Continuous-wave tFUS for 3 min (180 s) at 13 or 52 mW/cm2; electrophysiology recorded 2 min before, during the 3-min stimulation and 5 min after; at least 1 h between conditions.

flags.reason: Paper gives 'acoustic intensity' (13 and 52 mW/cm2) without naming Isppa or Ispta; CW so equal, recorded as isppa. Values are with a model rat skull in a water tank; no free-field values are given.
Pressures 14 and 28 kPa given at a 2 MHz center frequency; measured with a model skull (hydrophone), applied here to both transducers as the paper states them.
3 min CW stated; recorded as 180 s.

Two transducers (2.0 MHz Ultran, 2.5 MHz Sonic Concepts) used with identical protocols; results not split by frequency in the text, so four exposures (2 targets x 2 frequencies) share the same intensities.
Contralateral olfactory bulb has no matching target id; 'other' used.
FUS AIR: 1 cm air gap between transducer and skull; olfactory stimulation acts as off-target active control.
